claims.text: -l/--merge-logic defines how multiple annotation values are combined when several regions overlap a record
Rules are first, append, append-missing, unique, sum, avg, min, max with the stated meanings
sum applies to numeric fields only
avg applies to numeric fields only
The merge-logic option is experimental
It is intended for BED or TAB-delimited annotation files and works only when REF and ALT or BEG and END columns are present
Multiple rules can be comma-separated or given repeatedly

note: Context says numeric-only for sum only, not avg.

claims.text: Two tools in the context predict variant effects
VEP (based on Ensembl) determines effects of SNPs, indels, structural variants and CNVs
snpEff annotates and predicts effects of variants on genes, such as amino acid changes
VEP VCF header records software version and versions of databases such as ClinVar or dbSNP
VEP header describes the consequence annotation format in the INFO field
snpEff VCF header records software version and command line used
Oncotator is an older functional annotation tool developed by The Broad Institute
Funcotator and Oncotator are fundamentally different with some similarities
The author maintains a direct comparison should not be made
Funcotator is a functional annotation tool in the core GATK toolset
Funcotator labels each variant with one of twenty-three classifications
Funcotator annotates from data sources such as GENCODE, dbSNP, gnomAD and COSMIC

note: Well supported and appropriately hedged about which tool is newer.

claims.text: NGSCheckMate uses commonly heterozygous SNPs to detect sample mislabelling
NGSCheckMate output lists matched comparisons with correlation and a dendrogram
bcftools gtcheck checks sample identity; with -g query samples are checked against the -g file, without -g all query samples are cross-checked
Pairs can be selected with -p or -P
--n-matches limits output to the top matches
The discordance score equals mismatching genotypes only for GT-vs-GT matching
build_docker_remote.sh builds the GATK4 image using Google Cloud Build, useful if you cannot build locally
First run gcloud config set project <PROJECT> with a project that has Cloud Build access
Then run sudo bash build_docker_remote.sh -e ${GITHUB_TAG} -d ${STAGING_DIR}
The image is tagged us.gcr.io/broad-dsde-methods/broad-gatk-snapshots/gatk-remote-builds:<USERNAME>-<GITHUB_TAG>-<GIT_HASH> and uploaded to GCR
For gatkbase the remote script is build_docker_base_cloud.sh <docker_image_version>

note: Tag format is in h003, not cited h004.

claims.text: In a small tutorial dataset some annotations have insufficient data or no variance, so filtering options must be limited to a subset of annotations
The tutorial data include only 2 samples
Running VQSR on such a small dataset causes issues with some annotations, so the step uses fewer parameters
INDEL recalibrator uses -an QD -an FS -an SOR -an DP and SNP uses -an QD -an MQ -an FS -an SOR
vcfanno annotates a VCF with any number of INFO fields from any number of VCFs
vcfanno uses a simple configuration file specifying source files, fields and how they are added to the query VCF
SnpSift is set up with a CSV samplesheet of annotation databases
The -G option requires per-sample FORMAT/QS or FORMAT/AD tags generated by bcftools mpileup with -a QS or -a AD
A plugin is run like a normal command with its name prefixed by +, or as bcftools plugin NAME
General options come first, then --, then plugin-specific options
A normal command takes [OPTIONS] FILE, e.g. bcftools call '[OPTIONS] FILE'
Some plugins do not accept the common options and implement their own parameters
Examples are bcftools +counts in.vcf and bcftools plugin counts in.vcf

note: -G claim is in h026, miscited as h023.

claims.text: The GATK jar is at /gatk/gatk.jar inside the GATK4 docker image
build_docker_remote.sh builds the GATK4 image remotely with Google Cloud Build
Install git-lfs and run git lfs install
Run git lfs pull from the root of the GATK clone to download large test data, about 5 GB
A full git clone is required because the build needs git-lfs files in src/main/resources/large
These files are packaged inside the GATK jar and used by tools at runtime
A zipped source archive alone is not buildable
Files in src/test/resources/large are needed only by the test suite, not for building
For INDEL variants the FS threshold is FS > 200.0
For SNP variants the FS threshold is FS > 60.0
Both thresholds belong to hard-filtering procedure HF-01 and come from source gatk
HF-01 (HardFiltering) has the threshold SOR_gt_3 (SOR > 3.0, all variant types)
Seven thresholds are linked to HF-01: SOR_gt_3, FS_gt_200_indel, FS_gt_60_snp, MQRankSum_lt_-12.5, MQ_lt_40, QD_lt_2, ReadPosRankSum_lt_-8
The total may be eight

note: Eight is speculation; omitted neighbour not shown to be a threshold.
